title: The stalk of the normalization at a point is the integral closure in the product of residue fields of the minimal primes of the local ring

standard_prerequisites.name: The construction of the normalization and the identification of its pushforward of the structure sheaf by integral closures, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the identification of the stalk of the pushforward with the integral closure in a product of residue fields.

standard_prerequisites.name: An alternative description of the normalization, and the compatibility of integral closures with localization, cited from the same chapter and the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies a second route to the same identification, so that the two descriptions are seen to agree.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a reduced ring with finitely many minimal primes the product of the residue fields at those primes is the total ring of fractions
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the product appearing in the second description with the total ring of fractions of the reduced local ring.

core_obligations: Reduce to a convenient affine neighbourhood: replace the scheme by an affine open around the point in such a way that the scheme has finitely many irreducible components and the point lies in each of them (proof lines 14481-14484).

Identify the stalk of the pushforward: it is the integral closure of the local ring at the point in the product of the residue fields of the minimal primes of that local ring, by the construction of the normalization or, alternatively, by the description of the normalization together with compatibility of integral closures with localization (proof lines 14484-14489).

Identify the product with the total ring of fractions: the reduced local ring has finitely many minimal primes, corresponding to the generic points of the irreducible components through the point, so the product of the residue fields there is the total ring of fractions of that reduced ring, which is the third description (proof lines 14490-14501).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine neighbourhood whose components all contain the point and identify the stalk of the pushforward with the integral closure in a product of residue fields (proof lines 14481-14489).
Rewrite that product as the total ring of fractions of the reduced local ring, giving the third description (proof lines 14490-14501).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a scheme whose quasi-compact opens have finitely many irreducible components, the stalk of the normalization's pushforward at a point is canonically the integral closure of the local ring in the total ring of fractions of its reduction, equivalently in the product of the residue fields of its minimal primes (statement lines 14465-14479). The counted proof is short but complete: it passes to an affine neighbourhood whose components all contain the point, identifies the stalk with an integral closure in a product of residue fields via the construction of the normalization, and then rewrites that product as the total ring of fractions of the reduced local ring, using that the minimal primes correspond to the generic points of the components through the point (proof lines 14481-14501). It is H2: the argument is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the construction of the normalization and the comparison of products of residue fields with total rings of fractions.
